doc: With a (h, w) float32 per-texel offset (the surface terms' anomaly over the row sensitivity): compose is evaluated at mid[:, None] + offset, a float64 sum of a float32 array. Same dtypes and tolerance reasoning as solve_thresholds.typical.128x64. Arguments: s, fine, target, streak, subtexel and offset are the inputs of that name when listed; an unlisted streak or offset (default 0.0) is the scalar in params, an unlisted subtexel is None; prm holds the GenParams fields compose reads. The 36 steps and the bracket [-10, 10] are literals of the source. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 1.7e-8; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 6.4e-8 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is about 1e2x the larger of the two spreads.
